question: The meridian that roughly follows a ______ degrees longitude that passes through the mid-Pacific Ocean is called the International Date Line.
solution:
The correct answer is __**180.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The date line, also known as the **International Date Line**, is a line that marks the beginning of each calendar day.
 
• Through the** Pacific Ocean, the date line connects the North and South Poles.** But it isn't a straight line. 
 
• At **180 degrees, the antimeridian is halfway around **the globe. It is the foundation of the International Date Line. 
 
• Degrees east of the prime meridian are used to measure the** Eastern Hemisphere,** which makes up half of the globe. Degrees west of the prime meridian for the **Western Hemisphere, the other half.**
 
• In a system of **geographic coordinates**, the 180th meridian, also known as the **antimeridian.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **prime meridian's 180° meridian** extends from east to west.
 
• It is shared by both east longitude and west longitude and separates the **Earth into two hemispheres.**
 
• The **northern and southern**. It is not written in the** E or W forms** and has no direction.
